suggestions.title: Semiconductor Physics
suggestions.description_md: Semiconductor physics explains how crystalline materials with a moderate band gap give rise to controllable electrical behavior through doping, carrier transport, and junction formation. It bridges quantum mechanics and solid-state theory to explain why silicon can act as a switch, a diode, or an amplifier depending on how it is structured and biased. Anyone who wants to understand transistors, solar cells, or LEDs at a physical rather than circuit level needs this foundation.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: Builds on the condensed matter angle you flagged; band structure and statistical occupation are partition-function applications.

suggestions.title: Cosmology & the Lambda-CDM Model
suggestions.description_md: Cosmology is the study of the origin, structure, and evolution of the universe as a whole. The Lambda-CDM model is the current standard framework, combining cold dark matter and a cosmological constant (dark energy) to explain observations ranging from the cosmic microwave background to large-scale structure. Understanding it reveals how the universe expanded from a hot dense state, why galaxies cluster as they do, and what determines the universe's ultimate fate.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: Statistical mechanics underpins modern cosmology; phase transitions and critical phenomena appear in early-universe physics.

suggestions.title: Gravitational Waves & LIGO
suggestions.description_md: Gravitational waves are ripples in spacetime curvature produced by accelerating masses — most dramatically by merging black holes and neutron stars. LIGO and Virgo detect these signals using kilometer-scale laser interferometers sensitive to displacements smaller than a proton. Understanding this field spans general relativity, precision measurement, signal processing, and astrophysics, making it one of the richest intersections of theory and experiment in modern physics.
suggestions.why_suggested_md: Adjacent to the foundations you flagged.
